extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and other attorneys who practice before the USPTO; OED staff and parties involved in practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing the professional conduct, recordkeeping, client communications, filing responsibilities, and discipline/reinstatement processes for practitioners before the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO). Includes specific regulatory citations and examples of misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of competence (37 C.F.R. § 11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must provide competent representation to a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 as a basis for discipline; examples in the document include failing to timely pay filing fees, not taking reasonable steps to protect clients' interests, and filing applications that claimed priority to abandoned provisionals — conduct the OED Director viewed as inconsistent with competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of representation and allocation of authority (37 C.F.R. § 11.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must appropriately define and respect the scope of representation and the allocation of decision-making authority between client and practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as a rule the respondent was alleged to have violated; the Order's factual examples (e.g., failing to inform clients of abandonment or consequences of provisional filings) illustrate improper handling of responsibilities and client authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of diligence (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order identifies numerous failures: not submitting paid USPTO fees, not responding to USPTO notices, not responding to client inquiries over long periods — all cited as breaches of the duty of diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of communication (37 C.F.R. § 11.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must keep a client reasonably informed and promptly comply with reasonable requests for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: respondent did not inform clients of a Notice to File Missing Parts (NFMP) or a Notice of Abandonment, did not communicate contents of those notices, and failed to respond to client emails/phone calls about application status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties regarding communicating scope of representation, fees, and expenses (37 C.F.R. § 11.105(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must communicate the scope of representation and terms of fees/expenses to the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as a claimed violation; the Order notes failures related to client funds and lack of records that bear on fee handling and disclosure (e.g., collecting funds for fees but not remitting them and not maintaining records).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties to safekeep property and maintain required records (37 C.F.R. § 11.115)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must safekeep client property (including client funds) and maintain required records documenting client funds and their disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites failures to maintain the records required by § 11.115(f), not identifying the disposition of client funds paid but not remitted to the USPTO, and not returning client property (prototype) after repeated requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for client funds (37 C.F.R. § 11.115(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must keep records of client funds as required by § 11.115(f), identifying receipt and disposition of such funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent told OED he did not maintain the client-fund records required by 11.115(f) and could not identify the disposition of funds paid by clients but not remitted to the USPTO — cited as an aggravating factual basis for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties in terminating representation (37 C.F.R. § 11.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: When terminating representation, a practitioner must take reasonable steps to protect the client's interests (e.g., notify client, return papers/property, avoid prejudicing client).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order alleges respondent did not take reasonable steps in response to notices of missing parts/abandonment and failed to return a prototype despite repeated requests — examples of failing to comply with termination duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscribed conduct: dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation is prohibited and actionable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as one of the rules the OED Director opined were violated; the Order's factual allegations (e.g., receiving funds and not remitting fees and not informing clients) are presented as conduct raising issues under this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscribed conduct: prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the list of alleged violations; failures to properly pursue or protect clients' patent matters and to communicate could be characterized as prejudicial to the administration of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscribed conduct: other conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites this provision as among those the respondent was alleged to have violated; examples include not maintaining required records and not returning client property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to a Notice to File Missing Parts (NFMP) and avoiding abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: When the USPTO issues an NFMP specifying missing items (e.g., filing fees, surcharge, drawings, oath/declaration), the practitioner has the obligation to file the missing items within the NFMP-specified period (commonly two months) to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order quotes NFMPs that specified a two-month period to file missing fees and other items and notes respondent received or should have been aware of NFMPs but failed to respond, resulting in Notices of Abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to inform clients of USPTO notices and of application status
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must inform clients of USPTO notices (e.g., NFMP, Notice of Abandonment) and the status/consequences for their matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated factual allegations: respondent did not inform clients of NFMPs, did not communicate their contents, and did not inform clients that provisionals had been filed without fees or had gone abandoned; clients were unaware despite having paid invoices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to remit client funds for USPTO fees and to account for their disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: When a client provides funds to pay USPTO fees, the practitioner must timely remit those fees to the USPTO and maintain records accounting for the funds' disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order alleges respondent received funds for filing fees (both provisional and nonprovisional filings) and did not remit them, did not maintain records of these funds, and could not identify their disposition — a central factual basis for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to explain provisional vs non-provisional filing consequences and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must advise clients about the nature of provisional applications (not examined, do not by themselves yield patents), the need to file a non-provisional within one year to claim priority, and related deadlines and consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order alleges respondent failed to advise JEE Investments and inventors that provisionals are not examined, cannot yield a patent by mere filing, and that failure to file a non-provisional within one year can forfeit priority — factual failures relied on by OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to take reasonable steps to protect client interests when problems arise
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon learning of defects (e.g., missing fees, NFMPs, notices of abandonment), a practitioner must take reasonable corrective steps to protect the client's interests (e.g., notify client, file missing items, seek revival or extensions when appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order repeatedly states the respondent did not take reasonable steps after receiving NFMPs/Notices of Abandonment (e.g., did not file missing fees, did not notify clients, delayed or failed to file necessary documents such that petitions were dismissed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to return client property upon request (and after termination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must return client property (e.g., prototypes, papers) upon request and in accordance with terminating-representation duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order alleges respondent failed to return a prototype to JEE Investments despite repeated requests — cited as a violation of duties to protect client interests and safekeep/return property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for an Affidavit of Resignation and exclusion on consent (37 C.F.R. § 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit of resignation submitted for exclusion on consent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) and related provisions; the Director may approve an affidavit and order exclusion on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the respondent's Affidavit of Resignation complies with § 11.27(a) and therefore his exclusion on consent is approved. It also records respondent's acknowledgements (e.g., consent freely and voluntarily rendered, awareness of investigations) as part of the required content/effect of such an affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED investigations and notice procedures (37 C.F.R. § 11.22 referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Enrollment and Discipline may open investigations into potential violations under procedures referenced at § 11.22, and such investigations produce findings and opinions used in disciplinary actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order recites that the OED Director opened investigations and that the respondent was aware of them; the investigations produced factual allegations that informed the Director's opinion of rule violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for reinstatement applications (37 C.F.R. § 11.60 presumptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a practitioner who resigned under consent later applies for reinstatement under § 11.60, the OED Director may conclusively presume the facts and opinions from prior investigations are true for purposes of determining the reinstatement application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent acknowledged in the affidavit that OED would conclusively presume the allegations were true and that he could not have successfully defended against them when evaluating any future reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with conduct provisions during exclusion (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner excluded from practice before the Office must comply fully with the rules governing conduct during exclusion as set out in § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly orders respondent to comply fully with § 11.58; the citation signals regulatory obligations (e.g., regarding representation, use of title, etc.) while excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with reinstatement procedures (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner seeking reinstatement must follow the reinstatement procedures and requirements set out in § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires respondent to comply with § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement and notes the specific presumption applicable to his case as part of that process.
